overview: Black pushes 2...e4 against the fianchetto and White's knight goes to the rim on h4, aiming at f5 and g6 but offside. Black gains space with the e4 pawn and White hopes to undermine it with d3. The position is unclear and the knight on h4 may be harassed with ...g5.

white_ideas.idea: Undermine e4 with d3 and bring the knight back with Ng2 or Nf5
Use the long diagonal with Bg2
Aim to exploit the advanced e4 pawn

black_ideas.idea: Harass the h4 knight with ...g5 or ...Qxh4
Use the space to attack on the kingside

typical_structures.structure: Black e4/d5 centre against White's fianchetto

character.notes: The knight on h4 and Black's advanced pawn make the game unbalanced but not necessarily forcing.

structure.notes: Black has advanced the e-pawn, White hits it with d3; the centre is undecided.

level.notes: No long theory, but the knight on the rim needs care.

character.reason: It is unusual but not especially solid or forcing.

structure.reason: The centre is not yet settled.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose a knight on h4 here.

plans.reason: White fianchettoes and Black gains space with e4.
